Kling AI pricing and credits

Edited by Emmanuel Gonzalez

Some links on this page are affiliate links. Affiliate disclosure.

Official Kling membership plans, read Nov 14, 2026 from Kling membership plans, start at $6.99 for the first month of Standard (then $8.80/month; list $10.00/month) with 660 credits a month. The official API, from official API pricing document, charges $0.084/s at 720p without native audio ($0.84 per 10 seconds) and $0.126/s with native audio ($1.26 per 10 seconds). Those API figures match our catalog. The cheapest Kling 3.0 rate we track is $0.0225/s on Higgsfield (Ultra (annual), 720p, not stated). How many official app credits a clip uses is not published, so that conversion is not shown.

Last checked 2026-11-24. Official membership and API figures were read Nov 14, 2026. Catalog rows below use the date on each row. See the Kling 3.0 model page and the credit calculator for a 10-second Kling 3.0 clip.

Key takeaways

  • Cheapest catalog route. $0.0225/s on Higgsfield (Ultra (annual), tier Ultra (annual), 720p, not stated), checked Nov 24, 2026.
  • Cheapest verified pay-as-you-go rate. $0.0594/s on Magnific (1080p, not stated), checked Nov 22, 2026.
  • Official Kling API. $0.084/s at 720p without audio ($0.84 per 10s) and $0.126/s with audio ($1.26 per 10s), checked Nov 24, 2026.
  • Official app plans. From $6.99 first month ($8.80/mo ongoing) for Standard (660 credits/mo), checked Nov 14, 2026. Credits-per-clip is not published, so app plans are not converted to $/s.

    How much does Kling AI cost, and what do credits buy?

    On Nov 14, 2026, the official membership page listed Standard, Pro, Premier (with 8,000, 18,000, 28,000 or 38,000 credits a month), and Ultra+, plus a Business tab. Monthly plans show a one-time first-month price, then a lower-than-list ongoing monthly price. Yearly plans are billed once a year and grant the listed credits each month for 12 months. The figures are in the tables on this page, from https://kling.ai/app/membership/membership-plan.

    What do official Kling credits buy per second or per clip?

    That number is unknown. The official membership page lists how many credits each plan includes, and the cost per 100 credits, but it does not publish how many credits a Kling 3.0 or Kling 4.0 clip uses at a given resolution, with or without audio. This guide does not invent that conversion. Official API billing uses a separate resource-package unit priced in dollars on the API document, not the app credit packs. Benefits the page does list for paid plans include a generation queue, 1080p/4K video generation, watermark removal, and commercial use of generated content. It also mentions daily free credits for members and, during promotional periods, discounts that use fewer credits on eligible models, without a credits-per-clip table.

    How do official Kling credits work?

    The same terms, re-read Nov 18, 2026, distinguish plan credits from purchased credit packs. Credits that come with a paid plan are distributed each month and, as of those terms, are valid for 1 month from the date they are added to your account. Credits you buy (including auto-recharge purchases) are valid for 2 years from the date they are added. Credits with the shorter remaining validity period are used first. The official membership page still does not publish how many credits a Kling 3.0 clip uses, so this guide does not invent a cost per second from app credits. Source: Kling Terms of Paid Service, re-read Nov 18, 2026.

    How do I cancel a Kling paid plan?

    Kling's Terms of Paid Service, effective Oct 10, 2026, and re-read Nov 18, 2026, tell you to cancel a Stripe-billed plan in Stripe, an iOS plan in the iPhone or iPad Settings app or the App Store purchase history, and a Google Play plan in Google Play. After a paid plan is activated, fees are not refundable unless those terms specifically allow it. Turning off credit auto-recharge is a separate step inside Kling (Profile, then Credits, then Auto-Recharge Management) and does not cancel a paid plan.

    The official unsubscription steps in those terms are: for Stripe payments, use “Manage my subscription,” then “Cancel subscription,” then go to Stripe to manage the plan; for iOS 12 and above, open Settings, tap your name, open Subscriptions, choose the KLING AI plan, and tap Cancel Subscription (or cancel it from the App Store account purchase history); for older iOS, use Settings → iTunes Store & App Store → Apple ID → Subscriptions; for Google Play, open subscriptions, select the plan, and tap Cancel subscription. Source: Kling Terms of Paid Service, re-read Nov 18, 2026.

    Is Kling free?

    Kling sells paid Standard, Pro, Premier, and Ultra+ plans, which are listed on this page from the official membership page. The Terms of Paid Service, re-read Nov 18, 2026, describe those paid plans and do not describe a free plan. How many clips you can make without paying is not published as a credits-per-clip figure, so this guide does not invent a free-clip count. A short dedicated page on whether Kling is free is planned.

    What is confirmed, and what is not?

    Confirmed Nov 14, 2026 on official Kling pages: the membership plan prices, monthly credit allotments, first-month and ongoing monthly prices, yearly prices, credit packs, and the official API dollar rates for Kling 3.0 (and the other official API rows on the same document, which are not in this catalog). Confirmed in our catalog the same day: the third-party $/s rows in the comparison table, each with its vendor URL. Unknown: how many official app credits a clip uses, so an app-credit cost per second or per clip is not shown; whether the marketing page at https://kling.ai/pricing lists a different regional price (that URL rendered as a product page, not a plan table); and a Replicate Kling 3.0 rate, because we do not have one in the catalog.

    Confirmed Nov 14, 2026 on official Kling pages: Standard, Pro, Premier (four credit tiers), and Ultra+ monthly and yearly prices, first-month and ongoing monthly prices, credits per month, credit packs, the Business seat prices above, and the official API dollar rates for Kling 3.0. The membership page loaded without a login. Purchased-credit validity of 2 years is in the paid-service terms dated Oct 10, 2026.

    Confirmed in the catalog the same day: every third-party and official API $/s row in the comparison table, each with its vendor URL and checked date.

    Unknown: how many official app credits a Kling 3.0 or 4.0 clip uses, at any resolution, with or without audio, so an app-plan cost per second is not shown; a regional price, if any, that appears only after sign-in; a Replicate Kling 3.0 rate; and whether official API resource-package units can be mixed with app credits (the two price lists are presented as separate products).

    Affiliate links never change this price order.

    How do we calculate this?

    Each dollar figure is a current price row, with the vendor page and the date that page was checked. A published rate is a dollars-per-second figure on that page, or an API credit count times the credit price the page states. A credit-plan figure is plan price ÷ credits × credits per clip ÷ seconds, and it assumes every credit you pay for is used. When the vendor marks that count with "~", "roughly", or "estimated", the row is labelled estimated from credit plan and is not a list price. A promo shows its end date when the vendor gave one. The full method is on the about page.
